:::{#def-irreducible-error}
#### Residual variance

Let $\paren{\Predvar, \Outvar}$ be the [covariate](#def-covariate) and the outcome of one observation from a [population](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-population),
and let $\noise$ be its [noise](#def-noise).

The **residual variance** (or **irreducible error**) at the covariate value $\predvar$
is the [conditional population variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-cond-variance) of the noise given $\Predvar = \predvar$:

$$
\varpar \eqdef \Var{\noise \mid \Predvar = \predvar}.
$$ {#eq-irreducible-error}

It is a [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance), a component of the [expected squared prediction error](#def-epe), and not an error.
It is irreducible only given the [covariates](#def-covariate) the [prediction](prediction.qmd#def-prediction) uses:
a further covariate that [predicts](prediction.qmd#def-prediction) the outcome moves part of the spread out of the noise and into the [mean function](#def-mean-function),
so the residual variance depends on which covariates are measured.
Because $\Var{\noise \mid \Predvar = \predvar} = \Var{\Outvar \mid \Predvar = \predvar}$,
the residual variance averaged over the covariate values of [new observations](#def-new-observation) is $\E{\Var{\Outvar \mid \Predvar}}$.
It is a population quantity, not the [estimate](estimation.qmd#def-estimate) computed from the [residuals](prediction.qmd#def-residual) of a [fitted model](#def-fitted-model).

Source: @wikipedia_bias_variance_tradeoff;
@james2021islr2e [Section 2.2.2].
:::
